event.name: Contender Series: Season 10, Week 2
event.notes: "name" is matched as a substring against ESPN's own event name (punctuation and case are ignored), and the FIRST match in the scoreboard window wins. For a one-off card "UFC 330" is unique and enough. For a weekly series it is not: ESPN lists every Contender Series week inside the 45-day lookahead, so the name must carry the season and week or the run will silently price the wrong card. Discovery pulls recent uploads from each capper channel and keeps the ones whose title matches settings.discovery.title_contains. Add entries to "videos" only to pin a specific video by hand.

card.name: Dana White's Contender Series: Season 10, Week 2

comments.comment: Feels quite confident and doesn't mind parlaying Rodriguez: big speed and striking advantage over a very hittable Miller with sketchy durability.
Taking the untested Brazilian at face value — big, jacked, 27 and in his prime with a size advantage, while Miller looked cheeks on his last Contender Series appearance.
Rodriguez is better everywhere; Miller only has a power advantage and doesn't show much skill.
Called it a squash match and his top most confident pick — Rodriguez's explosive power striking is far too much for the outclassed grappler Miller.
Doesn't think either guy is UFC level, but expects the athletic, powerful Rodriguez to knock out the sloppy, non-durable Miller in round one and create a future fade opportunity.

Leaning Rodriguez as the better athlete and more dangerous striker; Miller is too hittable and his wrestling isn't good enough to justify the upset, so a head kick or hook along the fence finish is likely.
Crisp boxing combinations plus leg and body kicks should make Miller stationary and lead to a knockout.
Called his highest confidence pick of the card: Rodriguez has huge power in hands and kicks, Miller is shorter, hittable, with chin and cardio concerns after being battered by Goundry.
Miller is stiff, awkward and easily hit despite durability; Rodriguez is a decent, physically imposing striker who can walk him down and finish, likely in round one or two.
Trembley started MMA late, has faced nobody of note and mostly submits opponents, while Puga is a young Mexican knockout artist who has never been submitted.
Puga has great overall boxing and a purple belt in jiu-jitsu, with takedown defense and scrambling ability to handle Trembley's grappling.
Puga is the much better boxer with body work and professional boxing experience, and although his initial takedown defense is suspect he scrambles very well back to his feet.

Loves Puga's boxing, jab, hand speed and body work, and thinks his slick brown-belt jiu-jitsu will let him stay active off his back and get back to his feet against Trembley's clinch/wrestling pressure.
Puga is the crafty, slicker striker with solid takedown defense and good jiu-jitsu, so Trembly's wrestling shouldn't dominate and Puga should win the standup exchanges.

picks.selection: Douglas Rodriguez by KO in round 1

comments.comment: Believes Rodriguez finds Miller's chin early given the speed and power edge and Miller's questionable durability.
Rodriguez has size, power, speed and striking advantages similar to Ryan Gandra who battered Miller, but he warns not to max bet since Rodriguez is helpless off his back.
He expects Rodriguez to land big shots early and finish Miller in the first round.
Fasil's pressure and pocket-crashing should make Brito uncomfortable against the cage until one of the big shots flatlines him.
Favors Fasil in a striking battle because of better fundamentals when both tire; Brito starts well but gasses, and isn't a good enough wrestler to win that way.
Puga's boxing superiority against a hittable, aggressive Trembley who crashes the pocket; capper trusts Puga's grappling defense to stay out of trouble if taken down.
Puga is a legitimate boxing threat with striking finishes; Sam said he'll take the KO if it's plus money.
Trembley is very hittable and Puga's boxing should eventually put his lights out.
Puga is a pressure boxer who works the body and uses his size and reach well, and Tremblay's defense can be exposed; Puga can also scramble back up if taken down.

picks.selection: Roman Puga by KO in round 2

comments.comment: He expects Puga to set the finish up with body shots and get the stoppage in the second round.
He thinks Puga's boxing and body shots will accumulate on Tremblay and break him down in the second round.
Most competitive fight of the night, but Perez's own wrestling, jiu-jitsu and superior boxing should keep it standing where he wins.
Called Perez the lock of the card — far more skilled, showed the real deal against Manuel Sosa, while Paxton is a meat-and-potatoes wrestler who's beaten only tin cans.
Perez is notably faster on the feet and his grappling is strong, though Paxton's size and Perez's cardio issues are concerns.
Most confident pick and lock parlay leg: Perez has faced better competition and has solid striking plus a strong ground game, while Paxton built his record on cans.
Picks Perez by decision as the cleaner striker and grappler, but calls it a 'dog or pass' for betting purposes since Paxton's grinding wrestling could make it close and ugly.

picks.selection: Logan Paxton by TKO in round 3

comments.comment: Expects Paxton to wear Perez down (Perez gassed in round three of his prior DWCS fight) and get a late finish.
Fazil has the better overall skills and should have been in the UFC already, mixing takedowns with striking; Brito is a live dog though.
Fazil has the better submission game, a nice boxing base and high volume for three rounds; he should win if he keeps pressure and avoids fighting at Brito's distance.
Most confident pick and lock parlay leg: Fazil's forward pressure and combinations should overwhelm Brito, who he expects to slow down and crumble, possibly by TKO or club-and-sub.

picks.selection: Christian Perez by submission in the first two rounds

comments.comment: Perez is far more skilled and should cook Paxton, whose only path is takedowns and ground and pound.
Perez showed elite offensive grappling against Manuel Sousa and comes in off a short layoff, though Jacob is less confident due to Paxton's size, wrestling and likely good cardio.
He likes Perez's grappling after what he did to Manel Sousa early, but Perez gassed late so the finish should come in rounds one or two.
Expects Fazil to mix combinations and takedowns well and finish by knockout in a competitive fight.
